Grant Writer

Salary

Not Disclosed

Goodstack is an AI-native social impact startup backed by General Catalyst (investors in Stripe and Airbnb) that facilitated $5 billion in donations in 2025. They provide a unified platform for global brands like Google and OpenAI to integrate positive impact while supporting thousands of nonprofits with cutting-edge technology.

Job Description

Join Goodstack as a lead Expert Reviewer to help nonprofit partners secure funding faster. You will research high-quality grant opportunities, craft compelling funding narratives, and leverage AI tools to accelerate delivery. Working with 10–15 nonprofits simultaneously, you’ll ensure every application is funder-ready and persuasive to drive global social change.

Location

USA; Canada (Remote)

Why this role is remarkable

Directly impact global philanthropy by helping nonprofits like the Red Cross and Oxfam access the capital they need to thrive.
Work at the intersection of social good and cutting-edge technology within a General Catalyst-backed startup that facilitated $5B in donations in 2025 alone.
Master AI-native workflows that amplify your grant-writing craft, allowing you to focus on high-level strategy and persuasive storytelling rather than administrative overhead.

What You Will Do

Identify and curate tailored grant opportunities for 10–15 nonprofit partners based on their specific missions, eligibility, and funding requirements.
Draft and iterate on high-quality LOIs and grant applications, turning raw programme data into compelling, funder-ready narratives.
Lead the expert review process by quality-checking AI-assisted outputs to ensure every submission maintains the highest standards of accuracy and tone.

The ideal candidate

Demonstrated experience in grant writing for nonprofits or mission-led organisations with a deep understanding of the global funding landscape and eligibility criteria.
Exceptional analytical thinking and attention to detail, capable of navigating complex geographic nuances and strict funder requirements without error.
Technically proficient with AI tools for research and drafting, combined with the human judgment required to maintain warmth and clarity in partner communication.

Who are Jack & Jill?

Ok, I'll go first. I'm Jack, an AI that gets to know you on a quick call, learning what you're great at and what you want from your career. Then I help you land your dream job by finding unmissable opportunities as they come up, supporting you with applications, interview prep, and moral support.

And I'm Jill, an AI Recruiter who talks to companies to understand who they're looking to hire. Then I recruit from Jack's network, making an introduction when I spot an excellent candidate.

How does this work?

Jack's an AI agent for job searching and career coaching. He works for you.
Jill is the AI recruiter working for the company. She recruits from Jack's network.
If it's a match and the company wants to meet you, they'll make the intro. In the meantime, if you'd like, Jack will send you excellent alternatives.

We never post fake jobs

This isn't a trick. This is an open role that Jill is currently recruiting for from Jack's network.

Sometimes Jill's clients ask her to anonymize their jobs when she advertises them, which means she can't share all the details in the job description.

We appreciate this can make them look a bit suspect, but there isn't much we can do about it.

**This position is for our adolescent outpatient (PHP/IOP) location in Fairfax, VA**

Position Summary

The Behavioral Health Specialist (BHS) plays a vital, hands-on role in shaping the daily experience of adolescent and young adult patients in Newport Healthcare’s behavioral health programs. As a frontline team member, the BHS creates a safe, structured, and compassionate environment where patients feel supported, seen, and empowered throughout their healing journey. Newport Healthcare provides evidence-based treatment for mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and co-occurring challenges, with a focus on trauma, anxiety, depression, and family dynamics.

BHS roles exist across multiple levels of care
including 24/7 residential treatment and inpatient hospital settings
,
as well as outpatient/IOP/PHP
programs. While core responsibilities are consistent, workflows and acuity vary by setting; training and coaching are provided to ensure success in each environment. Schedules may include day, evening, overnight, weekend, and holiday shifts in a fast-paced milieu, and a BHS may need to respond to urgent or unique conditions during a scheduled shift.

This role isn’t just important; it’s foundational. BHS team members are the heart of our day-to-day care model, offering meaningful connection and stability that make a lasting difference in patients’ lives. Grounded in our core values of Patient First, Love, Excellence Through Integrity, Compassion, and Connection
, the BHS embodies our mission of helping young people move from struggling to thriving.

Key Performance Responsibilities

Create a safe and supportive space by offering consistent, compassionate care and supervision that ensures patients’ emotional and physical well-being.
Guide and encourage patients as they move through their day whether attending therapy, group activities, meals, or moments of transition.
Lead or support experiential activities (e.g., mindfulness, recreation, group engagement) that promote healing and connection.
Model calm, respectful behavior and healthy coping strategies in a way that builds trust and emotional safety.
Document observations and interactions clearly, accurately, and in a timely manner to support treatment planning.
Stay grounded and responsive during high-stress or emotionally charged situations, helping restore calm through established strategies.
Collaborate with team members and communicate professionally to support a connected, unified care environment.
Uphold ethical standards and confidentiality, maintaining patient dignity and respect in all interactions.
Participate in ongoing training and development provided to grow clinical understanding and ability to provide trauma-informed, values-based care.
Safely transport patients to and from program sites and external appointments (e.g., doctors, labs) following all safety standards and protocols.
Perform other duties as assigned.

What Makes You a Great Fit

Education, Experience, License Requirements:

High School Diploma or GED required.
Bachelor’s Degree in psychology, counseling, or sociology preferred.
Prior work experience in other behavioral treatment settings, a plus.
Must have a valid driver’s license and be eligible for insurance coverage for driving the company’s vehicles.
Must be minimum 21 years of age.
Must become CPI and CPR certified within the first 30 days.

Compensation for this role ranges from $17.70-$21.70 per hour depending on education and experience. 

We are committed to providing competitive and equitable compensation. An individual’s pay rate within the posted range is determined by several factors, including skills, experience, education, and market conditions. Additionally, we consider internal equity to ensure fairness within our organization.

Join Us

Join our vibrant team at Newport Healthcare, where your passion for helping adolescents and young adults can truly shine! If you’re looking for a rewarding role that combines creativity, compassion, and collaboration, this is the place for you!

jobs.title: Patient Care Coordinator
jobs.description:
Patient Care Coordinator — Are You the Person Who Makes Things Happen?

Full-Time | In-Person | Optimal Health

Some people wait to be told what to do.

Some people see what needs to happen — and make it happen.

We’re looking for the second person.

Optimal Health is a fast-growing chiropractic and physical therapy practice, and we’re looking for an exceptional Patient Care Coordinator to become one of the key people driving our patient experience.

We’re looking for someone who is:

Great with people.

Extremely organized.

Confident on the phone.

Comfortable with sales.

Competitive enough to care about results.

Detail-oriented enough that things don’t fall through the cracks.

And hungry enough to want more responsibility as they prove themselves.

If you’re looking for a job where you can sit behind a desk, answer a few phones, and wait for 5:00…

This isn’t it.

If you love people, move fast, communicate well, and get satisfaction from making things happen…

Keep reading.

The Mission

Our doctors and physical therapists can create an excellent plan for a patient.

But a great plan means very little if the patient doesn’t understand it, doesn’t schedule it, cancels appointments, disappears halfway through care, or never follows through.

Your job is to make sure patients don’t get lost.

You’ll become the quarterback of the patient journey — connecting patients with our doctors, therapists, clinical team, and front office.

You’ll know who needs a phone call.

Who needs to get scheduled.

Who cancelled.

Who hasn’t followed through.

Who has a question.

Who needs to talk to their doctor.

And who said, “I’ll call you later” three days ago and still hasn’t called.

You don’t wait for those problems to find you.

You find them first.

What You’ll Actually Do

You’ll spend your days:

Building genuine relationships with patients Talking with patients in person and on the phone Making outbound follow-up calls every day Helping new patients navigate their first few visits Supporting patients as they understand and commit to their treatment plans Helping patients work through scheduling, financial, and logistical concerns Following up immediately when patients begin falling off their care plan Re-engaging patients who have disappeared Keeping patients appropriately scheduled Coordinating chiropractic and physical therapy care Reinforcing recommendations made by our providers Recognizing when a question needs to go back to a doctor Tracking follow-ups so nobody falls through the cracks Helping our team deliver an exceptional experience in a high-volume practice

There is administration involved.

There are phones.

There is scheduling.

But those are tools of the job — not the purpose of the job.

The purpose is to own the patient experience and help people follow through.

Who We’re Really Looking For

Your resume matters less to us than who you are.

You’re a people person.

You can walk into a room and talk to almost anyone.

You remember names.

You ask good questions.

People tend to feel comfortable talking to you.

You’re great on the phone.

You don’t hide behind text messages.

Calling someone you’ve never met doesn’t bother you.

Neither does calling someone back for the third time because you said you would follow through.

You can sell.

Not the sleazy kind.

The good kind.

You listen.

You Figure Out What Someone Is Actually Concerned About.

You communicate value.

You ask good questions.

And you’re comfortable asking someone to make a decision.

You’re ridiculously organized.

If you tell a patient you’ll call Tuesday, you call Tuesday.

Nobody should need to remind you.

You have some competitive fire.

You like knowing whether you’re winning.

Goals don’t scare you.

Being measured doesn’t offend you.

You’d rather know where you stand and figure out how to improve.

You’re coachable.

We are building detailed training systems around patient communication, follow-up, sales, care-plan recovery, and the entire patient journey.

We’ll teach you.

But we’re going to expect you to learn it, practice it, and get good at it.

You take ownership.

This might be the most important one.

When something becomes yours, it’s yours until it’s finished.

Not: “I left them a voicemail.”

But: “Here’s where that patient stands, here’s what I did, and here’s what happens next.”

That’s the mentality we’re looking for.

Don’t Have Healthcare Experience?

That’s okay.

In fact, we’re open to someone completely outside healthcare.

We can teach you our systems.

We can teach you chiropractic.

We can teach you physical therapy.

We can teach you the patient journey.

We can teach you our approach to communication.

What is much harder to teach is energy, curiosity, ownership, work ethic, confidence, and the ability to connect with people.

You might come from:

Sales

Hospitality

Fitness or wellness

Recruiting

Customer service

Account management

High-end retail

Healthcare

Athletics

Leadership roles

Or somewhere we haven’t thought of

Recent college graduates are absolutely encouraged to apply.

If you’re early in your career but you’re sharp, hungry, organized, and great with people, we want to hear from you.

Why Optimal Health?

We’re not building an average healthcare office.

Optimal Health brings chiropractic, physical therapy, rehabilitation, and other treatment options together under one roof so our providers can work as a team.

We’re busy.

We’re growing.

And we’re actively building the people, training, and systems necessary to take the practice to another level.

That creates opportunity.

The person who earns this role won’t simply be another employee sitting at the front desk.

You’ll have real ownership.

You’ll work directly with doctors, therapists, clinical staff, and leadership.

You’ll learn healthcare.

You’ll learn communication.

You’ll learn sales.

You’ll learn how a growing practice operates.

And if you’re exceptional, there should be more opportunity for you as we continue to grow.

Your Schedule

This is a full-time, in-person position.

Healthcare doesn’t always fit neatly between 9:00 and 5:00, and neither does this role.

Our patient schedule includes some early mornings and evenings.

Some shifts may run until approximately 6:00–7:00 PM, but you will not work late every night.

Expect a mix of earlier and later shifts depending on patient volume and team coverage.

Some evening flexibility is required.

Compensation

Competitive hourly compensation based on experience, demonstrated ability, and fit.

There is also opportunity for performance-based bonuses after successful training and demonstrated competency.

We want someone who likes the idea that great performance creates greater opportunity.

Think You’re Our Person?

Don’t send us the same resume you’re sending to 50 other employers and hope for the best.

Show us.

We’re intentionally putting a small hurdle in the application process.

Why?

Because this job requires people who:

Read. Think. Learn. Communicate. Follow through.

Here’s your first chance.

The Optimal Health Challenge

Send Us Your Resume

Easy enough.

Do 10 Minutes of Homework

Visit our website: www.optimalhealth.fit

Find one treatment, technique, or service we offer that you didn’t know much about before today.

Then, in 150 words or less, tell us:

What is it?

How would you explain it in simple language to a patient who was nervous or confused about it?

Why did you choose that particular technique?

Don’t copy our website
.

We know what our website says.

We want to see how YOU communicate.

Now Show Us How You Think

Imagine this:

A patient is several visits into a treatment plan recommended by their doctor.

They cancel their next appointment and tell you:

“Honestly, I’m feeling a lot better. I don’t think I need the rest of these appointments. I’ll just call you if it starts hurting again.”

In 100 words or less, tell us how you would respond.

We’re not testing your medical knowledge.

There isn’t a secret clinical answer.

We’re looking for how you listen, think, ask questions, communicate, and handle a little resistance.

Prove You Pay Attention

At the very bottom of your application, write:

“I read the whole thing.”

If it’s missing, your application won’t move forward.

One Last Question

When you read this job description, did something in your head say:

“I’d crush this.”

Good.

We want to meet you.

Complete the challenge and apply.

Send us the information we asked for to: jess@optimalhealth.fit

If we want to move forward, we will contact you.

new_jobs.title: Patient Care Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
Patient Care Coordinator — Are You the Person Who Makes Things Happen?

Full-Time | In-Person | Optimal Health

Some people wait to be told what to do.

Some people see what needs to happen — and make it happen.

We’re looking for the second person.

Optimal Health is a fast-growing chiropractic and physical therapy practice, and we’re looking for an exceptional Patient Care Coordinator to become one of the key people driving our patient experience.

We’re looking for someone who is:

Great with people.

Extremely organized.

Confident on the phone.

Comfortable with sales.

Competitive enough to care about results.

Detail-oriented enough that things don’t fall through the cracks.

And hungry enough to want more responsibility as they prove themselves.

If you’re looking for a job where you can sit behind a desk, answer a few phones, and wait for 5:00…

This isn’t it.

If you love people, move fast, communicate well, and get satisfaction from making things happen…

Keep reading.

The Mission

Our doctors and physical therapists can create an excellent plan for a patient.

But a great plan means very little if the patient doesn’t understand it, doesn’t schedule it, cancels appointments, disappears halfway through care, or never follows through.

Your job is to make sure patients don’t get lost.

You’ll become the quarterback of the patient journey — connecting patients with our doctors, therapists, clinical team, and front office.

You’ll know who needs a phone call.

Who needs to get scheduled.

Who cancelled.

Who hasn’t followed through.

Who has a question.

Who needs to talk to their doctor.

And who said, “I’ll call you later” three days ago and still hasn’t called.

You don’t wait for those problems to find you.

You find them first.

What You’ll Actually Do

You’ll spend your days:

Building genuine relationships with patients Talking with patients in person and on the phone Making outbound follow-up calls every day Helping new patients navigate their first few visits Supporting patients as they understand and commit to their treatment plans Helping patients work through scheduling, financial, and logistical concerns Following up immediately when patients begin falling off their care plan Re-engaging patients who have disappeared Keeping patients appropriately scheduled Coordinating chiropractic and physical therapy care Reinforcing recommendations made by our providers Recognizing when a question needs to go back to a doctor Tracking follow-ups so nobody falls through the cracks Helping our team deliver an exceptional experience in a high-volume practice

There is administration involved.

There are phones.

There is scheduling.

But those are tools of the job — not the purpose of the job.

The purpose is to own the patient experience and help people follow through.

Who We’re Really Looking For

Your resume matters less to us than who you are.

You’re a people person.

You can walk into a room and talk to almost anyone.

You remember names.

You ask good questions.

People tend to feel comfortable talking to you.

You’re great on the phone.

You don’t hide behind text messages.

Calling someone you’ve never met doesn’t bother you.

Neither does calling someone back for the third time because you said you would follow through.

You can sell.

Not the sleazy kind.

The good kind.

You listen.

You Figure Out What Someone Is Actually Concerned About.

You communicate value.

You ask good questions.

And you’re comfortable asking someone to make a decision.

You’re ridiculously organized.

If you tell a patient you’ll call Tuesday, you call Tuesday.

Nobody should need to remind you.

You have some competitive fire.

You like knowing whether you’re winning.

Goals don’t scare you.

Being measured doesn’t offend you.

You’d rather know where you stand and figure out how to improve.

You’re coachable.

We are building detailed training systems around patient communication, follow-up, sales, care-plan recovery, and the entire patient journey.

We’ll teach you.

But we’re going to expect you to learn it, practice it, and get good at it.

You take ownership.

This might be the most important one.

When something becomes yours, it’s yours until it’s finished.

Not: “I left them a voicemail.”

But: “Here’s where that patient stands, here’s what I did, and here’s what happens next.”

That’s the mentality we’re looking for.

Don’t Have Healthcare Experience?

That’s okay.

In fact, we’re open to someone completely outside healthcare.

We can teach you our systems.

We can teach you chiropractic.

We can teach you physical therapy.

We can teach you the patient journey.

We can teach you our approach to communication.

What is much harder to teach is energy, curiosity, ownership, work ethic, confidence, and the ability to connect with people.

You might come from:

Sales

Hospitality

Fitness or wellness

Recruiting

Customer service

Account management

High-end retail

Healthcare

Athletics

Leadership roles

Or somewhere we haven’t thought of

Recent college graduates are absolutely encouraged to apply.

If you’re early in your career but you’re sharp, hungry, organized, and great with people, we want to hear from you.

Why Optimal Health?

We’re not building an average healthcare office.

Optimal Health brings chiropractic, physical therapy, rehabilitation, and other treatment options together under one roof so our providers can work as a team.

We’re busy.

We’re growing.

And we’re actively building the people, training, and systems necessary to take the practice to another level.

That creates opportunity.

The person who earns this role won’t simply be another employee sitting at the front desk.

You’ll have real ownership.

You’ll work directly with doctors, therapists, clinical staff, and leadership.

You’ll learn healthcare.

You’ll learn communication.

You’ll learn sales.

You’ll learn how a growing practice operates.

And if you’re exceptional, there should be more opportunity for you as we continue to grow.

Your Schedule

This is a full-time, in-person position.

Healthcare doesn’t always fit neatly between 9:00 and 5:00, and neither does this role.

Our patient schedule includes some early mornings and evenings.

Some shifts may run until approximately 6:00–7:00 PM, but you will not work late every night.

Expect a mix of earlier and later shifts depending on patient volume and team coverage.

Some evening flexibility is required.

Compensation

Competitive hourly compensation based on experience, demonstrated ability, and fit.

There is also opportunity for performance-based bonuses after successful training and demonstrated competency.

We want someone who likes the idea that great performance creates greater opportunity.

Think You’re Our Person?

Don’t send us the same resume you’re sending to 50 other employers and hope for the best.

Show us.

We’re intentionally putting a small hurdle in the application process.

Why?

Because this job requires people who:

Read. Think. Learn. Communicate. Follow through.

Here’s your first chance.

The Optimal Health Challenge

Send Us Your Resume

Easy enough.

Do 10 Minutes of Homework

Visit our website: www.optimalhealth.fit

Find one treatment, technique, or service we offer that you didn’t know much about before today.

Then, in 150 words or less, tell us:

What is it?

How would you explain it in simple language to a patient who was nervous or confused about it?

Why did you choose that particular technique?

Don’t copy our website
.

We know what our website says.

We want to see how YOU communicate.

Now Show Us How You Think

Imagine this:

A patient is several visits into a treatment plan recommended by their doctor.

They cancel their next appointment and tell you:

“Honestly, I’m feeling a lot better. I don’t think I need the rest of these appointments. I’ll just call you if it starts hurting again.”

In 100 words or less, tell us how you would respond.

We’re not testing your medical knowledge.

There isn’t a secret clinical answer.

We’re looking for how you listen, think, ask questions, communicate, and handle a little resistance.

Prove You Pay Attention

At the very bottom of your application, write:

“I read the whole thing.”

If it’s missing, your application won’t move forward.

One Last Question

When you read this job description, did something in your head say:

“I’d crush this.”

Good.

We want to meet you.

Complete the challenge and apply.

Send us the information we asked for to: jess@optimalhealth.fit

If we want to move forward, we will contact you.
